_budgets_comment: Master switch for the budget: the type and limit below. false (the default) checks nothing and keeps the values for when you turn it on (/tokentab:budget or the pane, the switch beside BUDGET on the Settings tab).
_unit_comment: Your account decides what a budget counts: percent of the plan's usage windows on Pro and Max, else USD (priced from prices.json). Only the budget type picked for that unit is checked.
_type_comment: The one budget checked, per unit, so switching accounts keeps each one's pick. usd: today (daily_limit_usd) or session (session_limit_usd). percent: today (the daily budget below, its cap weekly_limit_percent), week (weekly_limit_percent), five_hour (five_hour_limit_percent) or session (session_limit_usd, dollars at API rates). null (the default) takes the limit you had set: today in USD unless only the session limit is set; on Pro and Max today if the old daily budget switch was on, else week unless only the 5-hour limit is set.
_comment: Each budget type's limit; null disables it. Only the limit of the type in effect is checked.
_spend_less_comment: Beta. true also asks Claude to spend less (cheaper actions, shorter replies, and with hard_stop on, to wrap up) at each warning. false only warns you. null (the default) follows hard_stop, so stopping at the limit never cuts Claude off unwarned.
_daily_comment: On Pro and Max, budget type today: what is left of the week, spread evenly over the time left, fixed at the start of each local day. The week's own limit (weekly_limit_percent, else 100) is its cap.
_headline_comment: Which figure leads in the pane, the status line and the reopen button, counted as what is left: auto, session, today, five_hour or week. auto (the default) follows the budget type while the budget is on, else the week on Pro and Max (the daily budget if an older file's daily_budget.enabled is on) and today in USD. today is the daily budget on Pro and Max and today's spend in USD; five_hour and week are Pro and Max only, and a pick this account has no reading for falls back to auto. The status line shows at most two figures: the headline, then the budget, else the next figure.
headline: auto
_context_comment: Context size of the last call. Every call re-reads it all, so this is what each call costs. Warns once per threshold; resets after a compact.
_cold_comment: Blocks the first prompt after the prompt cache has expired, before anything is sent, when re-writing the context would be expensive. Sending again within confirm_seconds goes ahead. fresh_session_tokens estimates what a new session writes to start: the ~45k baseline plus ~30k re-read.
_handoff_comment: Shortly before a large context's prompt cache expires (write_at_minutes_1h / _5m after the last call, while the session sits idle and open), asks Claude once for a handoff note and saves it as handoff/<session>.md in the plugin's data folder. That one request reads the cache at the cheap rate. When you come back to a cold cache, the question above the prompt box offers to continue in a new chat from the note. Needs the session open and the computer awake.
_new_session_comment: Sends Claude the context size, cost per call and break-even for a new session with every prompt, so it can suggest one when the new prompt does not need this conversation.
_helpers_comment: Helper (subagent) tool calls get hard stops but not warnings and cannot start other agents unless helpers_may_delegate.
